Maya R.: heads-up — after yesterday's calibration change (use per-layer min/max stats) I'm seeing a perf regression on mixed-precision runs with continuous batching. p50 up ~12%, tokens/s down ~14% on the 8xA100 job :thinking_face:
Liam: ouch. which change exactly? the per-layer hist aggregate instead of global?
Maya R.: yes — we switched from a fast global calibration to per-layer s-curve (better quality) but the kernel selector seems to prefer FP32/FP8 fallbacks more often now. profiler shows extra memcpy + quant->dequant ops per batch. flame graph attached in perf-bot link.
perf-bot: perf dashboard -> https://internal.perf.redwood/team/eng-runtime/runs/1823456789 :bar_chart:
Serena: can you paste the gprof sample or the hot stack? quick glance at the dashboard shows KV cache hit ratio steady, so it's likely kernel choice / padding overhead not cache.
Maya R.: pasted flame snippet:
```
quantize_layer()  38%
memcpy(->device)  18%
run_kernel(fp8_kernel_fallback)  26%
batch_pack_padding  10%
```
Liam: batch_pack_padding at 10% stands out — are we packing by sequence length bins? continuous batcher may be mixing shapes so we pad to max that kernel supports.
Jonas: it's also possible the per-layer scale quant params change kernel shape selection. if a layer's scale is skewed we pick safer int8 path with extra branches.
Serena: can we repro with a controlled load? Maya, what's the request shape distribution?
Maya R.: mostly short prompts (avg 48 tokens) + a tail to 1024 for long-form. continuous batcher is combining short + long which causes large pad waste. I think the compounding effect is: per-layer calibration bumps some layers into fallback kernels AND large padding increases memcpy and reduces effective throughput.
Liam: two separate heuristics to try: (1) shape-aware batching: prefer small-only/long-only microbatches to reduce pad; (2) quant selection hysteresis: don't flip to fallback kernel unless regression > X ms for N windows.
Jonas: agree. also consider lazy quantize: delay quantization until kernel chosen or pack quantized buffers in-place to avoid extra memcpy.
Maya R.: quick experiment plan: A) run same trace with global calibration (old) vs per-layer and record kernel choice counts B) enable shape-aware batching in continuous_batcher (threshold 0.7 same-length) C) add simple hysteresis to kernel selector (+30% cost threshold). I'll run A and B first.
Serena: please capture the kernel_selector.log and kvcache stats. include per-layer quant param histograms.
Maya R.: will do. running batch of 10k requests now (synthetic) — command: `./perf/run_trace.sh --trace shortmix.json --iters 10000 --collect kernel_selector,memstats`
perf-bot: job queued (id perf-2026-03-18-22) :hourglass_flowing_sand:
Liam: FYI if hysteresis helps we should add unit tests that simulate shape churn and assert kernel stability.
Jonas: and add telemetry counters: kernel_switches_per_minute, pad_waste_tokens. that will make regressions easier to detect.
Maya R.: results summary (first 2k iters): global-calib p50=142ms, per-layer p50=160ms. kernel switches increased from 0.9 -> 2.5 per 1000 requests. pad_waste_tokens went from 18% -> 23%. attaching logs to the perf job.
Serena: OK that's actionable. Maya can you try enabling shape-aware batching with bucket threshold 0.6 and re-run the per-layer calibration case?
Maya R.: starting that run now. ETA ~45m. will post raw numbers when done. :thumbsup:
Liam: great. if that doesn't close the gap we should consider a hybrid quant path: per-layer calibration for accuracy, but fall back to a cached global scale for the kernel decision stage to avoid flapping.
Jonas: and note: if we introduce hysteresis, pick decay window relative to sequence length distribution — longer sequences tolerate less switching.
Maya R.: noted. will include suggestions in the follow-up PR. thanks all.
